summary: Selena M-26 is a realistic, modular lunar orbital observatory and landing site navigator designed to overcome the extreme illumination and radio blackout challenges of the Lunar South Pole. Built from 4 standardized cylindrical modules (4.5m diameter) launched via SpaceX Falcon Heavy / Starship and inserted onto a fuel-saving Free-Return Trajectory by a jettisonable booster stage, the station hosts a dedicated crew of 10 scientists and engineers. Combining Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), autonomous AI, and NASA LRO QuickMap, Moon Trek, and Artemis III data, Selena M-26 generates real-time "Traffic-Light" landing maps (Green/Yellow/Red). To safely explore permanently shadowed craters like Shackleton, it deploys low-cost, expendable Arduino impact probes that measure water ice, temperature, and slope, relaying short-range data to the station overhead before downlinking to Earth. Funded by B2B cargo/lab leasing and radar mapping, the mission reaches break-even in ~14 voyages.
details:
Selena M-26 (Selene, Greek goddess of the Moon + M for Moon + 26 for 2026) is an integrated cislunar research station and Lunar South Pole Landing Site Navigator engineered for modern heavy-lift launch systems.

Realistic Architecture & Orbital Mechanics:

* 4 Cylindrical Modules (4.5m diameter): Sized to fit inside SpaceX Falcon Heavy / Starship payload fairings (with crew rotation via Crew Dragon / Orion), replacing retired Space Shuttles: (1) Cargo & Probe Dispenser, (2) Science Lab & SAR Radar, (3) Crew Habitat for 10 Researchers & 50-cm Water Radiation Shelter, and (4) Fused-Quartz Observation Cupola & 360° Rotating Solar Array.

* Free-Return Trajectory & Jettisonable Booster: A 5th propulsion cylinder injects Selena M-26 onto a lunar free-return trajectory and detaches cleanly (ODAR-compliant, zero dead weight), using lunar gravity to return toward Earth with near-zero propellant consumption and high-bandwidth data downlink.

Data, Sensors & Hardware Prototype:

* Lunar Site Navigator: Cross-references NASA LRO QuickMap, Moon Trek 3D, and Artemis III candidate region data with onboard SAR scans to classify landing sites (Green/Yellow/Red) based on solar power and Earth radio windows.

* Expendable Arduino Impact Probes: Micro-probes dropped into permanently shadowed craters like Shackleton measure water ice, cryogenic temperature, and terrain slope upon impact. Because small probes lack the power to transmit 384,000 km to Earth, they transmit short-range telemetry to Selena M-26 overhead, which stores and relays the data once back in Earth visibility.

B2B Commercial Sustainability:

With 0 tourists and 100% scientific payload capacity, Selena M-26 costs €850M to build/launch (CAPEX) and €6M per 18-day mission (OPEX). By leasing cargo bays and modular Plug & Play lab racks to space agencies and pharma (€55M/mission) and selling SAR landing maps (€12M/mission), it generates +€61M net profit per mission, reaching break-even in ~14 missions under strict Outer Space Treaty compliance.
